title: Auto-merge AI-generated dependency updates — Project Northstar (next 4-week cycle)
question: Should Project Northstar enable automatic merging for AI-generated dependency updates during the next release cycle (four weeks)?
verdict: Enable automatic merging only for low-risk, patch-level dependency updates that match the controlled-replay conditions, after adding signed provenance and rollback drills; do not enable blanket auto-merge for all AI-generated updates during the next cycle.

nodes.label: Provisional position
nodes.text: Enable automatic merging only for low-risk, patch-level dependency updates that match the controlled-replay conditions, after adding signed provenance and rollback drills; do not enable blanket auto-merge for all AI-generated updates during the next cycle.

nodes.label: Controlled replay results (R1)
nodes.text: In the synthetic replay, 18 of 20 low-risk patch updates passed the complete test suite without manual edits. The two failures were detected before merge by the required checks.
nodes.claim: Most low-risk patches passed tests in replay

nodes.label: Replay boundary (R2)
nodes.text: The replay did not include major-version updates, packages with install scripts, or changes that modified authentication and authorization code.

nodes.label: Missing signed provenance (S1)
nodes.text: The fixture has no signed provenance record for generated pull-request descriptions. A reviewer therefore cannot verify from the description alone which model, prompt, or retrieved advisory produced a recommendation.

nodes.label: Proposed rule scope (S2)
nodes.text: The proposed rule currently excludes neither packages with install scripts nor updates that touch the authentication directory.

nodes.label: Review queue delay (O1)
nodes.text: The synthetic team recorded a median wait of 31 hours for routine patch-update review during the previous four-week cycle.

nodes.label: No rollback drill recorded (O2)
nodes.text: No rollback drill has been recorded for an automatically merged dependency update. The fixture contains no measurement of recovery time after a bad merge.

nodes.label: Unknown recovery time after bad auto-merge
nodes.text: No measurement of recovery time after a bad automatically merged dependency update exists in the fixture; the operational cost and recovery time are therefore unknown and could change the decision.

edges.note: High pass rate in the synthetic replay (18/20) increases reason to allow auto-merge for low-risk, patch-level updates that match replay conditions.
Replay explicitly excluded major-version updates, install-script packages, and auth-related changes, so auto-merge should be limited to the classes included in the replay.
Absence of signed provenance means automated merges could proceed without verifiable origin information, which contradicts enabling auto-merge without additional provenance controls.
The proposed rule does not exclude packages with install scripts or auth-dir changes; allowing those would contradict a safe auto-merge policy.
Median 31-hour review wait for routine patch updates supports automating merges for routine low-risk patches to reduce delay.
No recorded rollback drill is the evidence underlying the unknown: there is no measurement of recovery time after a bad merge.
Absent recovery-time measurements could reverse or narrow the decision; without them, risk of automatic merging is incompletely assessed.
